You don’tbuy a BMS.You specify it.

Romania’s BACS obligation for non‑residential buildings with over 290 kW of heating or air conditioning has been due since 31.12.2024. What the law requires, what it costs, and what to write into the specification so you are not tied to one supplier.

• Legal obligation

Two thresholds.Two legal regimes.

31.12.2024

290 kW

Law 372/2005 (Romania)

Deadline passed: the obligation already applies.

Non‑residential buildings, effective rated output per system family (heating, air conditioning or combined with ventilation), where technically and economically feasible.

31.12.2029

70 kW

Directive (EU) 2024/1275

Not yet transposed into Romanian law: not a domestic obligation today.

Transposition deadline: 29.05.2026. On 15.07.2026 the Commission sent letters of formal notice to all 27 member states.

Law 238/2024 raised the fines under Law 372/2005 by up to about 400%.

• Guide · Building management systems03 / 13

• Definition

It measures.It controls.It records.

A BMS is the layer of control and measurement between a building’s services (heating, ventilation, air conditioning, lighting, pumps, metering) and the people responsible for them.

Without it, each piece of plant runs in isolation: the boiler only knows the boiler, the chiller only knows the chiller, and nobody knows whether both are running at once on an April day.

In law it is BACS, building automation and control systems: the same technical object. Not to be confused with the other BMS, battery management system.

• Architecture

Three levels.Each with its own cost risk.

L3Supervision

Server, operator station (HMI), licences.

Licences are the most often forgotten budget line.

L2Automation

DDC controllers and the automation panel.

Spare point capacity: at least 15–20%.

L1Field

Sensors, actuators, valves, meters.

CO2 sensors drift out of calibration in 2–3 years.

• Guide · Building management systems05 / 13

• Concepts

Five concepts.The key to any specification.

  1. 01

    Data point

    A value with an address. The unit of measure of a BMS project.

  2. 02

    Control loop

    Measure, compare with the setpoint, act. Tuning decides whether the plant is stable.

  3. 03

    Sequence of operation

    How the plant behaves in every state. The most important document, and the most often missing.

  4. 04

    Schedule

    The operating calendar. The cheapest saving in a building.

  5. 05

    Interlock

    A non‑negotiable condition: the fan does not start until the damper is open.

• Protocols

Six protocols.A ten‑year commercial decision.

BACnetThe backbone: controllers, AHUs, chillers
ModbusThird‑party equipment: chillers, UPS, power analysers
KNXLighting, blinds, room control
DALIAddressable luminaires
M‑BusHeat, water and gas meters
LONDeclining; common in buildings fitted out 2000–2015

• Guide · Building management systems07 / 13

• Openness

A closed systemlooks fine in year one.

It shows in year five, when the owner wants 40 more points for a refitted floor and gets a single quote.

• The minimum to write into the specification

  • Native BACnet/IP at automation level
  • Modbus integration for third‑party equipment
  • Full handover of point maps and the software project
  • Licences in the client’s name

• Mistakes

Eight mistakesthat keep coming back.

01

A specification copied from another project

02

A system sized to the last point, with no spare

03the most expensive

Commissioning cut from the budget

04

Poorly configured alarms: at 400 a day, all ignored within two weeks

05

Meters installed without communication

06

A closed system, accepted without anyone noticing

07

Missing or token as‑built documentation

08

Nobody in the organisation responsible for the system

A system installed but never tuned uses as much as no system at all. And one tuned in August is not tuned for January.

• Guide · Building management systems11 / 13

• Before signing

Ten questionsfor the integrator, answered in writing.

  1. 01Which protocols are native, and what goes through a gateway?
  2. 02Who owns the licences, and what do 200 more points cost in year five?
  3. 03Is the software project handed over editable, with backups?
  4. 04Who writes the sequences of operation, and when can they be seen?
  5. 05How many commissioning hours are included, and what is tested?
  6. 06How much spare point capacity does the design have?
  7. 07Who answers at 2 a.m., how fast, and what does the contract say?
  8. 08Three similar buildings commissioned by the proposed team, not just the company?
  9. 09What happens if the supplier disappears?
  10. 10Who has remote access, and how?

Save this list. Under 15% spare points: paid changes from year one.

• By role

What it meansfor each role.

01Owner and investor

Lower regulatory risk, a protected asset value. First internal question: what rated output is installed across the portfolio?

02Facility manager

The quick win is running it properly: real schedules, cleaned‑up alarms, retuned loops, failed points fixed.

03Technical director

The win is in the specification: native open protocols, the software project handed over, licences in the client’s name, with the expansion price fixed upfront.

Send this to the colleague in the right role.
